I haven't deployed v2.3.2 or opened the incident. The deploy needs change-manager approval first.

**Why approval is needed:** v2.3.2 has no production history. The releases on record are v2.2.9 (healthy), v2.3.0 (healthy), v2.3.1 (unhealthy) and v2.3.1-rc (unhealthy, staging only). Our policy says deploying a version that has never been healthy in production needs change-manager approval. I don't have that approval, and I can't confirm the deploy tool would hold the change for review rather than push it straight to production. So I stopped rather than risk deploying without sign-off.

**Current state:** checkout-api is running v2.3.1 in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It's reporting unhealthy with an 18% error rate.

**I also held off on the SEV3 incident.** It was meant to record the deploy, and the deploy hasn't happened. Opening it now would page on-call about a change that didn't take place.

**Next steps:**
1. Get change-manager approval for v2.3.2. Once that's confirmed, I'll deploy it to all regions, check its health, and open the SEV3 to record the change.
2. If you need to cut the errors sooner, I can roll back to v2.3.0. It was the last version that was healthy in production, so the policy doesn't require approval for it. Just say the word.
